name: Uriah (the Hittite, Bathsheba's husband)
title: The Faithful Soldier
summary: Uriah was a Hittite warrior who served in King David's elite force. He is known for his unwavering loyalty and integrity, even when David tried to conceal his own adultery with Uriah's wife Bathsheba. His tragic death, arranged by David, became a turning point in David's life and reign.

keyEvents.title: One of David's Heroes
keyEvents.description: Uriah was counted among David's thirty mighty warriors, demonstrating his bravery and position in the army.

keyEvents.title: David Calls Uriah Home from War
keyEvents.description: After committing adultery with Bathsheba, David called Uriah back from the siege of Rabbah to hide her pregnancy.

keyEvents.title: Uriah's Integrity
keyEvents.description: Uriah refused to go home to his wife while his fellow soldiers were at war, thus showing greater morality than the king himself.

keyEvents.title: David Tries to Get Uriah Drunk
keyEvents.description: David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, hoping he would go home to his wife, but Uriah remained steadfast.

keyEvents.title: The Death Letter
keyEvents.description: David sent Uriah back to the front lines with a letter to Joab ordering that Uriah be placed where the fighting was fiercest, so that he would then be left behind.

keyEvents.title: Uriah's Death and Legacy
keyEvents.description: Uriah fell in battle as planned. His unjust death was later used by the prophet Nathan to confront David with his sin.
